reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents BitClub Network as a paid bitcoin-mining opportunity tied to passive income, recruitment, team purchases, and commission payments. It claims potential earnings of $60,000 per month and practically inexhaustible income over a thousand-day period, while directing viewers to register or contact someone to obtain the stated results. The claims, payments, and outcomes are not verified.

citations.quote: Once buying products with BitClubNetwork, you will receive a steady growing fair passive income.
there are three options packages they are 500 dollars, 1000 dollars and 2000 dollars
When you connect 1 and 2 people who want to do the business or just become the customers of this project You get 5% of each purchase their share inside the company
all passive income that your company makes day by day from your equipment is divided into two parts
when you invite a person he begins to receive his passive income

opening.argument: The presentation does not document a completed payment, accepted contract, or guaranteed outcome. Its language describes a proposed opportunity and projected mechanics: the speaker says participants “will receive” income after buying products, while the displayed mining page includes a contract period and a warning that the contract becomes effective only after a delay. That supports treating the material as an offer requiring independent evaluation, not as proof that viewers will receive returns. The account page shows a displayed balance, but a balance screen alone does not establish its source, withdrawal, or profitability.

citations.quote: Once buying products with BitClubNetwork, you will receive a steady growing fair passive income.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats promotional projections as verified results. The cited income language describes what the plan claims, not a demonstrated payment to the viewer. Likewise, the cited packages and percentages identify purchase options and proposed commission rules, but do not establish that anyone deposited money, recruited successfully, or received the claimed amounts. The thousand-day language describes a stated operating period, not proof of a scam outcome.

citations.quote: one place at the start you have a limit of $800 a day or $24,000 a month.
team that supplies you with equipment that you're going to work with for the next 1000 days

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a completed withdrawal does not neutralize the solicitation. The presentation explicitly says buying products produces passive income, and it presents a delayed mining contract rather than a neutral risk disclosure. The warning visible on the page does not explain that the promised returns are unreliable, and the account balance does not verify that the displayed funds came from mining or could be withdrawn.

citations.quote: Once buying products with BitClubNetwork, you will receive a steady growing fair passive income.

opening.argument: The video can be read as an operational walkthrough of how a platform’s plans, pools, bonuses, rankings, and account screens function. It explains the three package options, shows a binary-team diagram, presents qualification tables, and displays a wallet interface. The narration repeatedly describes mechanics rather than showing a viewer completing a purchase or receiving a withdrawal. A tutorial or demonstration may explain a controversial service without independently certifying every claim about it.

citations.quote: there are three options packages they are 500 dollars, 1000 dollars and 2000 dollars

rebuttal.rebuttal: The material is not merely descriptive commentary. It calls the plan unique, highlights income, explains how to qualify, and directs interested people toward obtaining the stated result through the supplied link. Explaining a system can still be promotional when the explanation emphasizes earnings and participation. The presence of diagrams and account pages does not by itself change that commercial context.

citations.quote: How to get this result you can learn from the the person who gave you a link to this video.
the bit club network has several types of revenues, these are quick money, middle money and long money for you

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough becomes promotional when it presents the opportunity as producing income and invites viewers to pursue the result. This video says the system has “quick money, middle money and long money,” describes a registration fee and paid packages, and links recruitment to commissions. Tables and interface screenshots document the sales mechanism; they do not make the claims educational or verified.

citations.quote: these are quick money, middle money and long money for you
The company cost $99, this is a one-time fee
When you connect 1 and 2 people who want to do the business or just become the customers of this project You get 5% of each purchase

opening.argument: The most concrete evidence is an advertised product-and-service arrangement: the page offers mining pools priced at $500, $1,000, and $2,000, and the narration describes equipment, contracts, account balances, and service bonuses. The supplied material does not show a viewer entering payment details, accepting terms, receiving a withdrawal, or being asked for credentials. Referral percentages may be ordinary promotional compensation attached to purchases rather than proof that the underlying service is fictitious. On this record, the mechanism is asserted but not independently tested.

citations.quote: there are three options packages they are 500 dollars, 1000 dollars and 2000 dollars
from each purchase, you will receive from 10 to 18%

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the packages a service does not resolve the income structure attached to them. The presentation says participants buy products to obtain passive income, and it ties payments to inviting people and their purchases. The absence of a shown transaction is not evidence that the advertised mechanism is ordinary or legitimate; it simply means the video makes the pitch before any transaction is shown.

citations.quote: Once buying products with BitClubNetwork, you will receive a steady growing fair passive income.
When you connect 1 and 2 people who want to do the business or just become the customers of this project You get 5% of each purchase

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is not whether a service can have packages or referral marketing. The issue is that the presentation links paid packages to passive bitcoin income, describes earnings from team purchases, and advertises an allegedly inexhaustible stream. The lack of a shown payment or withdrawal does not support ordinary commerce; it leaves the promised returns unverified while the sales pitch supplies the central evidence.
